proposed_from.topic: Study exactly bivariate stationary Gaussian OU systems dX_t=-A X_t dt+D^{1/2}dW_t with known bidirected support, trace(D)=1, D diagonal and strictly positive, kappa I <= Sigma <= kappa^{-1} I, |A_12| and |A_21| at least eta, ||A||_F <= M, and iid stationary snapshots. Prove an exact characterization of the compatible sign set of A_12 A_21 using the affine Lyapunov fiber and four finite sector certificates, including explicit witnesses and every open-versus-closed attainment branch. Derive the equal-variance thresholds, exhibit an open region where neither edge sign is identified but their product sign is, and analyze the explicit asymmetric zero-diffusion contact. Invert a covariance confidence region with a measurable nearest-model fallback to obtain honest finite-sample set coverage, uniform singleton recovery beyond root-n clearance, and a matching local Gaussian lower bound on compact contact subcharts. Exclude larger-graph projection, marginalization, global boundary-distance equivalence, and empirical-performance claims. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The affine Lyapunov parametrization yields explicit scalar sector-feasibility rules: u A_12+s A_21=t[s+(u-s)d]/(2 Delta), exact same-sign strict-feasibility branches, always strictly feasible opposite-sign polygons, and a closed-form equal-variance norm after x=d-1/2 and y=q+rx/2. These reductions give positive and negative thresholds, including unattained norm equality. At the asymmetric contact, g >= (s-u)td is necessary and d=g/[2(s-u)t], q=(eta Delta-dt/2)/s constructs positive witnesses for g>0. Symbolic algebra and 400 randomized active-set comparisons supported these unverified derivations. Checks covered empty K, kappa=1, t=0, s=u, margin equality, norm equality, zero-diffusion contact, fixed-alpha empty covariance regions, and local-versus-global boundary distance; no verified current-literature collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently prove completeness of the finite equality-active-set certificate and its scalar J and strict-attainment branches on every rank-deficient, lower-dimensional, and norm-equality sector. EARLY KILL TEST: Exactly certify the asymmetric g=0 J-false contact, an attained equal-variance positive threshold, and the r=1/2, eta=3/5, M^2=67/45 unattained negative infimum; any failure stops this theorem spine. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest published result is van Seeventer and Salehkaleybar's one-edge signature-set theory: its target is \(\operatorname{sign}(A_e)\), its decisive construction allows a single target edge to equal zero, and its graph-level extension is left open. Their work supplies the positive diagonal diffusion context, not the trace-one convention. The selected kernel first quotients the elementary common scaling \( (A,D)\mapsto(cA,cD)\) by choosing \(\operatorname{tr}(D)=1\); it then maps the observed covariance into \(\operatorname{sign}(A_{12}A_{21})\) under edge and drift-norm bounds \(\eta\) and \(M\) expressed in that normalized time unit. Dettling, Homs, Améndola, Drton, and Hansen prove that a directed two-cycle destroys global drift injectivity when diagonal volatility is fixed, but they do not ask whether a nontrivial sign functional is constant on that fiber. The finite sector certificate, strict-attainment topology, equal-variance thresholds, and zero-diffusion contact are therefore new mathematical objects rather than a relabeling of either comparator. The inference layer is also absent from the OU sign literature: generic set inversion does not supply the measurable fallback or the contact-specific upper and lower recovery theory.

seed_details.anchor: vanSeeventerSalehkaleybar2026, Theorem 4.2, Remark 5.1, and Conclusion; DettlingHomsAmendolaDrtonHansen2023, Example 3.2 and Theorem 4.3
seed_details.live_opportunity: Replace one-edge zero feasibility by a necessary-and-sufficient characterization of the product-sign image of the directed two-cycle fiber.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After half-vectorizing the Lyapunov equation, retain its one-dimensional nonidentification direction and impose four joint sign sectors, strict diffusion positivity, edge margins, and a quadratic norm cap instead of testing one edge at zero.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for \(\operatorname{sign}(A_{12}A_{21})\), cycle polarity, loop polarity, and bivariate Lyapunov sign identification returned no exact product-sign certificate beyond the one-edge anchor.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from van Seeventer and Salehkaleybar because their edge-sign feasibility program can be run twice.
seed_details.rebuttal: Separate edge feasibility does not determine joint sign compatibility; the new object requires simultaneous sectors and exact strict-attainment analysis under a shared diffusion allocation and norm cap.
seed_details.burned_reason: The single bivariate OU polarity angle was mathematically sound but structurally below the field floor; the proposed all-boundary extension is a separate research program.

seed_details.anchor: DettlingHomsAmendolaDrtonHansen2023, affine fiber construction in Section 3; vanSeeventerSalehkaleybar2026, strict positive diagonal diffusion in Definition 2.3
seed_details.live_opportunity: Classify every attained, closure-only, and infeasible branch when an affine Lyapunov fiber meets sign halfspaces and a drift-norm ball.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace generic rank and algebraic-identifiability arguments by a complete face-rank analysis of a strictly convex quadratic over each closed sector, followed by an interior-diffusion interpolation test.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining strict diffusion, active-set attainment, bounded Lyapunov fiber, and cycle signs found generic identifiability and optimization papers but no boundary-sensitive classification.
seed_details.red_team: This is elementary two-variable quadratic programming with no causal content.
seed_details.rebuttal: The causal conclusion changes at equality because strict positive diffusion removes closed minimizers; the full equality stratification is exactly what decides whether a polarity is observationally compatible.

seed_details.anchor: vanSeeventerSalehkaleybar2026, Definition 2.8 and Conclusion; ChernozhukovHongTamer2007, confidence-region inversion for identified sets
seed_details.live_opportunity: Construct an honest random set for the full compatible polarity set when the constrained OU covariance image is nonclosed.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Invert a regular covariance confidence ball through existential sector feasibility and add a measurable nearest-model rule on empty intersections, rather than bootstrapping the discontinuous sign-set map.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for OU sign confidence sets, Lyapunov identified-set inference, and covariance-region inversion found no model-specific construction handling strict-diffusion nonclosure.
seed_details.red_team: Coverage is a tautological projection of a covariance confidence set.
seed_details.rebuttal: Coverage is simple on nonempty intersections, but uniform singleton recovery fails without a measurable fallback and a certificate-specific clearance analysis because the model image need not be closed.

seed_details.anchor: vanSeeventerSalehkaleybar2026, positive-measure partial-identification construction; Hansen2025Trek, variance-inequality arguments
seed_details.live_opportunity: Exhibit and characterize a smooth polarity transition caused solely by one diffusion coordinate approaching zero.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Solve the same-sign sector at equality, isolate the scalar contact function \(g\), and prove that its sign controls entry into the legal fiber despite strict norm slack.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for zero-diffusion contact, OU sign frontier, and Lyapunov polarity boundary found no such explicit contact theorem.
seed_details.red_team: A single algebraic covariance witness is a hand-tuned curiosity.
seed_details.rebuttal: The witness seeds a smooth codimension-one surface with two open adjacent regimes and uniform local geometry, not an isolated counterexample.

seed_details.anchor: Kaji2021, weak regularity and local asymptotic risk; vanSeeventerSalehkaleybar2026, population sign trichotomy
seed_details.live_opportunity: Determine the sharp local separation order for honest singleton recovery near regular OU polarity contacts.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Identify the normal covariance displacement to the semialgebraic contact, embed it in the Gaussian covariance LAN experiment, and compare testing risk across adjacent identified and ambiguous regimes.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for minimax OU sign recovery, local Lyapunov polarity inference, and Gaussian covariance contact testing found general weak-identification theory but no OU-specific rate result.
seed_details.red_team: Root-\(n\) follows automatically because covariance is regular.
seed_details.rebuttal: Regular covariance estimation alone does not identify the relevant normal direction, relate it to set clearance, or prove an honest-procedure lower bound across a nonclosed polarity contact.

seed_details.anchor: Hansen2025Trek, explicit variance inequalities; vanSeeventerSalehkaleybar2026, covariance-level edge-sign conditions
seed_details.live_opportunity: Derive exact positive and negative polarity thresholds on the equal-variance covariance slice, including unattained norm equality.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Rotate diffusion allocation and circulation to \((x,y)\) coordinates that diagonalize the norm objective before imposing the joint sectors.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for equal-variance OU cycle signs and bivariate Lyapunov closed-form thresholds found variance-order results only for acyclic drift.
seed_details.red_team: A symmetric slice is merely an illustrative special case.
seed_details.rebuttal: The slice exposes qualitatively distinct attained and unattained equality branches and provides exact kill tests for the general certificate.

seed_details.anchor: vanSeeventerSalehkaleybar2026, Remark 4.5 on positive-measure partial edge-sign identifiability
seed_details.live_opportunity: Show on a relatively open covariance region that neither edge sign is identified although their product sign is.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Construct both opposite-sign orientations with common strict slack, then separately exclude both same-sign sectors through the joint elimination identity.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for joint-only feedback sign identification and graph-level OU sign quotients found no open-region result.
seed_details.red_team: The product is identified only at the isolated covariance \(I_2\).
seed_details.rebuttal: Strict witness slack and a strict exclusion inequality extend the conclusion to an open neighborhood of \(I_2\).

seed_details.anchor: ReckeHansen2026, higher-cumulant generic drift identification; DettlingHomsAmendolaDrtonHansen2023, Gaussian two-cycle nonidentification
seed_details.live_opportunity: Characterize the discontinuity between Gaussian polarity-set inference and non-Gaussian full-drift recovery as higher cumulants vanish.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Embed the cumulant equations in a local sequence whose third-or-higher cumulants approach zero and derive when full-drift inference collapses to the Gaussian polarity quotient.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for vanishing-cumulant Lyapunov identification and weakly non-Gaussian OU inference found the endpoint papers but no transition frontier.
seed_details.red_team: This is a routine weak-signal version of Recke and Hansen.
seed_details.rebuttal: A valid result would require a new joint limit experiment and an exact reduction to the Gaussian sign-set target, but it is less directly supported than the selected bounded-fiber kernel.
